steps.what: Verify applicable government-issued certification requirements and complete necessary renewal or maintenance activities
outputs: maintained certification evidence or unresolved renewal needs

tasks.design: Retain personal completion of required certification activities and checks against issuing authority information in {DOCS}. A reminder can signal a date but cannot establish competence or renew a certificate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements depend on actual duties, certificates and the responsible authority.
tasks.enabler_now: The provided logbook evidence does not establish certification maintenance automation.
tasks.still_hard: Training, examinations and evidence requirements may require personal participation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a gap and complete the actual requirement rather than rely on a stored expiry date.
tasks.altitude: Certification responsibility and personal activity time remain unchanged.

reach.role: captain, mate or pilot of water vessels
reach.task: Clarify certification required for an assigned duty
reach.learn: How actual duties affect qualification requirements

evidence.claim: Certification maintenance includes personal compliance activities; no measured local automation saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is the sailor's certification maintenance, excluding authority adjudication and employer-wide credential administration. Exact national and vessel requirements remain to be verified locally.

Authorities supply current requirements and certificate evidence before s1 closes; the sailor checks duty applicability and completes or arranges required activities within retained time. No free qualification-current or renewal-complete flag is assumed; unresolved requirements receive manual clarification.
Use existing official information and native reminders first. No new system, delegated data capture or added upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Actual vessel, duty and issuing authority requirements
research_questions: Which certification requirements demand personal attendance or additional evidence?

already_counted.description: Requirement checking and personal certification maintenance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Personal certification maintenance remains human work; no reminder administration share is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Stand watch to identify obstructions and locate navigational aids in the ship's surroundings
outputs: reports to the responsible watch officer

tasks.design: Retain the sailor's lookout watch and direct reporting under existing vessel instructions in {DOCS}. Electronic logs do not replace observation of the actual surroundings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Obstructions and navigational aids must be recognized in changing visibility and context.
tasks.enabler_now: The supplied evidence concerns log keeping and establishes no automatic lookout replacement.
tasks.still_hard: Partial visibility and ambiguous observations require attention and timely communication.
tasks.human_edge: Notice something unexpected and communicate uncertainty to the responsible officer.
tasks.altitude: Protect continuous lookout attention and reporting time.

reach.role: captain, mate or pilot of water vessels
reach.learn: Which context the responsible officer needs with a report

evidence.claim: Electronic logbook capability does not establish replacement of lookout watch or a local observation-time saving.

assumptions: Boundary is sailor lookout and reporting, excluding navigation decisions and vessel control.

The responsible officer supplies the watch assignment before s1; the sailor produces observations during the watch before reporting. Observation and clarification remain within retained time; no free obstacle-detected, navigational-aid-identified or clear-path flag is assumed.
Existing watch arrangements and direct communication remain the means. No new sensing system or transferred work is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual watch arrangements and reporting responsibilities
research_questions: Which observation uncertainties need immediate clarification with the watch officer?

already_counted.description: Continuous lookout, interpretation and direct reporting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Live lookout remains necessary and logbook case figures are not transferred.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read gauges and record engineering data

steps.what: Read pressure and temperature gauges and capture identified readings, units and observation times
Format captured pressure and temperature data into draft engineering log entries
Check readings and accept the exact engineering log contribution for responsible officer review

tasks.design: Use native electronic log templates in {OPS_SYSTEM} after the oiler reads and captures each observation. Avoid recopying the captured values into the formal entry; preserve engineer review and any required signing through the existing process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observed values can be copied repeatedly into log layouts.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic logbook products support structured entries; a usable sensor interface is not assumed for these gauges.
tasks.still_hard: A reading can be unclear, incorrectly identified or inconsistent with the actual equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize an uncertain observation and refer it rather than silently normalize it.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeat transcription while retaining physical reading and acceptance.

reach.learn: How observation identity and context affect log interpretation

evidence.claim: NAPA Logbook supports electronic engineering logs with automation and sensor inputs; this design uses manual source capture unless a supported feed is verified.
The manual-capture and template design's labour shares are E1, with no physical reading saving claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is oiler observation and log contribution, excluding engineer diagnosis and official signing. Existing engineer review remains unchanged; the oiler does not assume the engineer's authority. Acceptance of electronic records for this exact vessel and log must be confirmed before rollout.

Gauges produce readings during s1 and the oiler captures equipment/gauge ID, observation timestamp, pressure/temperature value, unit, context and explicit uncertainty there. Its 55 hours include direct inspection and all entry; no free telemetry feed or valid-reading flag exists. S2 only formats those captured facts. Unsupported gauges, missing fields or unaccepted electronic logs use manual logging.
OPS_SYSTEM means the vessel's operational log system. Native templates precede custom code. No new engineer signoff duty is added; new integration support is counted below.
unknowns: Exact log acceptance, native capture support and repeated copying workload
research_questions: Does single capture reduce total log effort after direct gauge reading, exceptions and existing engineer review?

already_counted.description: Physical reading and structured observation capture
Exact log contribution checking and acceptance

incremental.description: Entry template checks and failed-entry follow-up

approvals.approved_version: Exact equipment IDs, times, values, units, uncertainty remarks and source observations recorded as the oiler contribution; changes require renewed acceptance and existing engineer review.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=75, gross=25, focal upkeep=8, net=17. Range 0-5 allows existing single-entry logs, unsupported vessel approvals and minimal repeat copying; physical reading remains retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record weather and distance in ship logs

steps.what: Verify weather and distance source observations and capture the ship log input
Record captured weather and distance fields in the specified ship log template
Check and accept the exact ship log contribution for watch officer review

tasks.design: Use native structured entries in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the vessel log system, to format verified weather and distance observations once. The sailor checks the contribution and the watch officer retains existing review and signing; unsupported observations remain manually recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Known observations are copied and formatted into repeated log entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic deck logbooks can handle structured records without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Observation timing, source differences and record acceptance vary by vessel and log type.
tasks.human_edge: Identify what the observation actually supports and retain uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated log formatting while retaining source verification and responsibility.

reach.role: captain, mate or pilot of water vessels
reach.task: Review a source discrepancy in the deck log
reach.learn: Why source time and observation context matter to the official record

evidence.claim: NAPA Logbook provides deck logbooks and structured automation inputs, with flag-specific acceptance limits in the digest.
The Anthony Veder case reports fleet paperwork reduction with unclear period and inconsistent headline figures; no reported percentage is transferred to this task.
Local single-capture log savings remain an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is sailor log recording, excluding navigation calculations performed by officers, lookout watch and official officer signing. Existing officer review is unchanged. Confirm acceptance of the actual electronic log before use.

Existing vessel instruments and responsible observers produce available weather and distance information before s1 capture; no new source system is assumed. During s1 the sailor captures vessel/watch ID, observation time and source time, source identity, weather field values/units, distance value/unit and context or uncertainty. Its 45 hours include reading sources, clarification and manual entry. No free verified-weather, synchronized-feed or valid-distance flag exists; missing or incompatible sources and unaccepted log types use manual entries.
Native log templates precede custom code. Shared source capture with other log or watch tasks is assigned once; no new structured reporting duty is transferred to the officer.
unknowns: Actual electronic deck log acceptance and duplicate-entry burden
research_questions: How much log formatting remains after source reading, time checks and officer review?
